passages.text: Then Hezekiah sent word throughout all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh inviting them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover of the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah.
Hezekiah also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh.
He invited the people to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
He invited them to keep the Passover of the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וְגַֽם־ אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ עַל־ אֶפְרַ֣יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לָב֥וֹא לְבֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת פֶּ֔סַח לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For the king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month, since they had been unable to observe it at the regular time, because not enough priests had consecrated themselves and the people had not been gathered in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
King Hezekiah ruled in Jerusalem.
Hezekiah had officials and a large assembly with him.
Hezekiah, his officials, and all the people in Jerusalem made a decision.
They decided to keep the Passover in the second month.
They could not keep the Passover at the regular time.
Not enough priests had consecrated themselves.
The people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּעַ֨ץ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֛יו וְכָל־ הַקָּהָ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִֽי׃ כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יָכְל֛וּ לַעֲשֹׂת֖וֹ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא כִּ֤י הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ לֹֽא־ הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמַדַּ֔י וְהָעָ֖ם לֹא־ נֶאֶסְפ֥וּ לִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: This proposal pleased the king and the whole assembly.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah heard the proposal.
The proposal pleased Hezekiah.
The assembly was in Jerusalem.
The proposal pleased the whole assembly.
passages.original: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: So they established a decree to circulate a proclamation throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that the people should come to keep the Passover of the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem. For they had not observed it as a nation as prescribed.
passages.sermon:
The leaders in Jerusalem made a decision.
They decided to send out a message to all Israel.
They sent this message from Beersheba in the south to Dan in the north.
They called all the people to come to Jerusalem.
They told the people to keep the Passover.
The Passover is for the LORD, the God of Israel.
The people had not kept the Passover as God commanded.
They had not done it as a whole nation for a long time.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲמִ֣ידוּ דָבָ֗ר לְהַעֲבִ֨יר ק֤וֹל בְּכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִבְּאֵֽר־ שֶׁ֣בַע וְעַד־ דָּ֔ן לָב֞וֹא לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּ֛סַח לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָרֹ֛ב עָשׂ֖וּ כַּכָּתֽוּב׃

passages.text: So the couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his officials, which read: “Children of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that He may return to those of you who remain, who have escaped the grasp of the kings of Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Couriers carried letters.
The king and his officials sent these letters.
The couriers traveled through all Israel and Judah.
The king commanded the couriers to deliver a message.
The message said, “Children of Israel, return to the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel.
If you return to Him, He will return to you.
He will return to those of you who remain.
You have escaped from the kings of Assyria.”
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ הָרָצִ֨ים בָּֽאִגְּר֜וֹת מִיַּ֧ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֗יו בְּכָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּכְמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָם֙ יִצְחָ֣ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיָשֹׁב֙ אֶל־ הַפְּלֵיטָ֔ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֣רֶת לָכֶ֔ם מִכַּ֖ף מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Do not be like your fathers and brothers who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He made them an object of horror, as you can see.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of your fathers.
Your fathers and brothers were unfaithful to Him.
They betrayed the LORD.
God punished them.
He made them an object of horror.
You can see what happened to them.
Do not be like your fathers and brothers.
passages.original: וְאַל־ תִּֽהְי֗וּ כַּאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְכַ֣אֲחֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָעֲל֔וּ בַּיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם לְשַׁמָּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתֶּ֥ם רֹאִֽים׃

passages.text: Now do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did. Submit to the LORD and come to His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever. Serve the LORD your God, so that His fierce anger will turn away from you.
passages.sermon:
The king of Judah sent a message to the people of Israel and Judah.
He spoke to the children of Israel.
He said, “Do not be stubborn like your fathers.
Do not harden your necks as your fathers did.
Submit yourselves to the LORD.
Come to His sanctuary.
God has set apart this sanctuary forever.
Serve the LORD your God.
If you do this, the LORD will turn away His fierce anger from you.”
passages.original: עַתָּ֕ה אַל־ תַּקְשׁ֥וּ עָרְפְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם תְּנוּ־ יָ֣ד לַיהוָ֗ה וּבֹ֤אוּ לְמִקְדָּשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדִּ֣ישׁ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וְעִבְדוּ֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְיָשֹׁ֥ב מִכֶּ֖ם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and sons will receive mercy in the presence of their captors and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and merciful; He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD is gracious.
The LORD is merciful.
If you return to the LORD, He will not turn His face away from you.
If you return to the LORD, your brothers will receive mercy from their captors.
If you return to the LORD, your sons will receive mercy from their captors.
If you return to the LORD, your brothers will return to this land.
If you return to the LORD, your sons will return to this land.
passages.original: כִּ֣י בְשׁוּבְכֶ֞ם עַל־ יְהוָ֗ה אֲחֵיכֶ֨ם וּבְנֵיכֶ֤ם לְרַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י שֽׁוֹבֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָשׁ֖וּב לָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את כִּֽי־ חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹא־ יָסִ֤יר פָּנִים֙ מִכֶּ֔ם אִם־ תָּשׁ֖וּבוּ אֵלָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: And the couriers traveled from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun; but the people scorned and mocked them.
passages.sermon:
Couriers carried a message.
They traveled from city to city.
They went through the land of Ephraim.
They went through the land of Manasseh.
They traveled as far as Zebulun.
The people saw the couriers.
The people scorned the couriers.
The people mocked the couriers.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְי֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים עֹבְרִ֨ים מֵעִ֧יר׀ לָעִ֛יר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וְעַד־ זְבֻל֑וּן וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ מַשְׂחִיקִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וּמַלְעִגִ֖ים בָּֽם׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: Some men lived in Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun.\r\nThese men humbled themselves.\r\nThey came to Jerusalem.
passages.original: אַךְ־ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מֵאָשֵׁ֥ר וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וּמִזְּבֻל֑וּן נִֽכְנְע֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: Moreover, the power of God was on the people in Judah to give them one heart to obey the command of the king and his officials according to the word of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people in Judah lived in the land of Judah.
God acted with power among the people in Judah.
God gave the people in Judah one heart.
The people in Judah became united in purpose.
God caused the people in Judah to obey the command of the king.
God caused the people in Judah to obey the command of the king’s officials.
The king and his officials gave their command according to the word of the LORD.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם בִּיהוּדָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ יַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֑ד לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: In the second month, a very great assembly gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
passages.sermon: A very great assembly gathered in Jerusalem.\r\nThis happened in the second month.\r\nThe people came to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
passages.original: וַיֵּֽאָסְפ֤וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עַם־ רָ֔ב לַעֲשׂ֛וֹת אֶת־ חַ֥ג הַמַּצּ֖וֹת בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י קָהָ֖ל לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: They proceeded to remove the altars in Jerusalem and to take away the incense altars and throw them into the Kidron Valley.
passages.sermon:
The people in Jerusalem acted together.
They removed the altars in Jerusalem.
They also took away all the incense altars.
They threw the altars into the Kidron Valley.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֕מוּ וַיָּסִ֙ירוּ֙ אֶת־ הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ הַֽמְקַטְּרוֹת֙ הֵסִ֔ירוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֖יכוּ לְנַ֥חַל קִדְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And on the fourteenth day of the second month they slaughtered the Passover lamb. The priests and Levites were ashamed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered in Jerusalem.
They came to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
On the fourteenth day of the second month, they slaughtered the Passover lamb.
The priests and the Levites felt ashamed.
The priests and Levites consecrated themselves.
They brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֤ם נִכְלְמוּ֙ וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ עֹל֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They stood at their prescribed posts, according to the Law of Moses the man of God. The priests sprinkled the blood, which they received from the hand of the Levites.
passages.sermon:
The priests and Levites served in the temple in Jerusalem.
They followed the Law of Moses.
Moses was a man of God.
The priests stood at their assigned places.
The Levites handed the blood to the priests.
The priests sprinkled the blood.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַמְד֤וּ עַל־ עָמְדָם֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם כְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ זֹרְקִ֣ים אֶת־ הַדָּ֔ם מִיַּ֖ד הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

passages.text: Since there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves, the Levites were in charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for every unclean person to consecrate the lambs to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Many people in the assembly had not consecrated themselves.
These people were not clean.
The Levites took charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for them.
The Levites did this for every unclean person.
The Levites consecrated the lambs to the LORD.
passages.original: כִּי־ רַבַּ֥ת בַּקָּהָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־ הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם עַל־ שְׁחִיטַ֣ת הַפְּסָחִ֗ים לְכֹל֙ לֹ֣א טָה֔וֹר לְהַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: A large number of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover, contrary to what was written. But Hezekiah interceded for them, saying, “May the LORD, who is good, provide atonement for everyone who sets his heart on seeking God—the LORD, the God of his fathers—even if he is not cleansed according to the purification rules of the sanctuary.”
passages.sermon:
Many people were present in Jerusalem.
Most of these people came from the tribes of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun.
These people had not purified themselves.
They ate the Passover meal.
They did not follow what was written in the Law about purification.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed for these people.
Hezekiah said, “May the LORD, who is good, forgive everyone who sets his heart on seeking God.”
Hezekiah called the LORD the God of their fathers.
Hezekiah asked for forgiveness even for those who were not cleansed according to the rules of the sanctuary.
passages.original: כִּ֣י מַרְבִּ֣ית הָעָ֡ם רַ֠בַּת מֵֽאֶפְרַ֨יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה יִשָּׂשכָ֤ר וּזְבֻלוּן֙ לֹ֣א הִטֶּהָ֔רוּ כִּֽי־ אָכְל֥וּ אֶת־ הַפֶּ֖סַח בְּלֹ֣א כַכָּת֑וּב כִּי֩ הִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב יְכַפֵּ֥ר בְּעַֽד׃ כָּל־ לְבָב֣וֹ הֵכִ֔ין לִדְר֛וֹשׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֥ים׀ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֖א כְּטָהֳרַ֥ת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD for the people.
The LORD listened to Hezekiah.
The LORD healed the people.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּרְפָּ֖א אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃ס

passages.text: The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, and the Levites and priests praised the LORD day after day, accompanied by loud instruments of praise to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were in Jerusalem.
They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
They celebrated for seven days.
They had great joy.
The Levites praised the LORD every day.
The priests praised the LORD every day.
They used loud instruments to praise the LORD.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶת־ חַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וּֽמְהַלְלִ֣ים לַ֠יהוָה י֣וֹם׀ בְּי֞וֹם הַלְוִיִּ֧ם וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים בִּכְלֵי־ עֹ֖ז לַיהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: And Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites who performed skillfully before the LORD. For seven days they ate their assigned portion, sacrificing fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites.
These Levites served skillfully before the LORD.
The Levites ate their assigned portion for seven days.
They sacrificed fellowship offerings during these days.
They gave thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עַל־ לֵב֙ כָּל־ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הַמַּשְׂכִּילִ֥ים שֵֽׂכֶל־ ט֖וֹב לַיהוָ֑ה וַיֹּאכְל֤וּ אֶת־ הַמּוֹעֵד֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים מְזַבְּחִים֙ זִבְחֵ֣י שְׁלָמִ֔ים וּמִ֨תְוַדִּ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: The whole assembly agreed to observe seven more days, so they observed seven days with joy.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered in Jerusalem.
They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
They celebrated for seven days with great joy.
After this, the whole assembly made a decision.
They agreed to celebrate for seven more days.
They observed these seven days with joy.
passages.original: וַיִּוָּֽעֲצוּ֙ כָּל־ הַקָּהָ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ שִׁבְעַת־ יָמִ֖ים שִׂמְחָֽה׃

passages.text: For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for the assembly, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep for the assembly, and a great number of priests consecrated themselves.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
Hezekiah gave animals to the assembly.
Hezekiah gave one thousand bulls.
Hezekiah gave seven thousand sheep.
The officials also gave animals to the assembly.
The officials gave one thousand bulls.
The officials gave ten thousand sheep.
Many priests set themselves apart for holy service.
passages.original: כִּ֣י חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְ֠הוּדָה הֵרִ֨ים לַקָּהָ֜ל אֶ֣לֶף פָּרִים֮ וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֣ים צֹאן֒ס וְהַשָּׂרִ֞ים הֵרִ֤ימוּ לַקָּהָל֙ פָּרִ֣ים אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֖אן עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ כֹהֲנִ֖ים לָרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Then the whole assembly of Judah rejoiced along with the priests and Levites and the whole assembly that had come from Israel, including the foreigners who had come from Israel and those who lived in Judah.
passages.sermon:
The people of Judah gathered together as an assembly.
The priests were there.
The Levites were there.
People from Israel also came to the assembly.
Foreigners who had come from Israel joined them.
People who lived in Judah were present too.
All these people rejoiced together.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֣וּ׀ כָּל־ קְהַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֗ה וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְכָל־ הַקָּהָ֖ל הַבָּאִ֣ים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהַגֵּרִ֗ים הַבָּאִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהַיּוֹשְׁבִ֖ים בִּיהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: So there was great rejoicing in Jerusalem, for nothing like this had happened there since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was king of Judah.
He led the people in a great celebration.
There was great rejoicing in Jerusalem.
The people had not seen such joy in Jerusalem for a long time.
Nothing like this had happened since the days of Solomon.
Solomon was the son of David.
Solomon was king of Israel.
passages.original: וַתְּהִ֥י שִׂמְחָֽה־ גְדוֹלָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֠י מִימֵ֞י שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן־ דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א כָזֹ֖את בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Then the priests and the Levites stood to bless the people, and God heard their voice, and their prayer came into His holy dwelling place in heaven.
passages.sermon:
The priests and the Levites stood up.
They blessed the people.
God heard their voice.
Their prayer reached God's holy dwelling place in heaven.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשָּׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם וַתָּב֧וֹא תְפִלָּתָ֛ם לִמְע֥וֹן קָדְשׁ֖וֹ לַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃פ
